title: Ethiopian Tamarind Sweet
community: Southern and eastern Ethiopia — the tamarind confection
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Tamarind Sweet — tamarind paste cooked with honey and cardamom until thick, rolled in sesame seeds. The tart-sweet confection of Ethiopia's tamarind-growing regions — intensely flavoured, with the same sweet-sour-spice balance that characterises the best Ethiopian food.
longDesc: Tamarind grows in Ethiopia's lowland and Rift Valley areas, and the tamarind sweet is the traditional confection of those regions — the intense tartness of tamarind balanced with Ethiopian honey and cardamom produces a flavour unlike any other.
ingredients: // Rolling: sesame seeds or desiccated coconut
steps: Combine tamarind, honey, sugar, and cardamom in a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring, 12—15 minutes until very thick.
Test: a drop cooled on a plate should not spread.
Roll in sesame seeds or coconut.
chefTips: Very thick — it should barely pour when done.
Cool slightly before rolling — too hot is impossible to handle.
commonMistakes: Too thin — sticky balls that don't hold shape.
cookingScience: Tamarind's tartaric acid (the dominant organic acid) reacts with the honey's sucrose during cooking — producing a mixture that sets differently from pure honey candy, with a softer, more chewy texture due to the acid's effect on sugar crystallisation.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian lowland tamarind — wild-harvested or farmed.
healthBenefits: Tamarind is very high in B vitamins.
culturalNote: Ethiopian tamarind sweet is the tart-sweet confection that captures the essential balance of Ethiopian food philosophy — in a cuisine that masters the combination of heat, sourness, and richness, even the desserts carry this complexity.
